title: JACUSA2 downstream labels: use real condition names, not hard-coded WT/ADAR1KO
description: JACUSA2.py exports under literal keys 'WT'/'ADAR1KO' positionally (bases1*->'WT', bases2*->'ADAR1KO') and Multiple-Analysis.py hard-codes conditions=['WT','ADAR1KO'] + panel labels 'WT condition'/'ADAR1KO condition' + 'if condition==ADAR1KO'. So config1=ADAR1KO/config2=WT yields swapped/mislabeled panels. Fix: patcher rewrites both scripts to use real condition1/condition2 names (bases1*=condition1, bases2*=condition2) when JACUSA2 enabled. Disabled path unchanged.
close_reason: Patcher now re-keys JACUSA2.py export and relabels Multiple-Analysis.py (conditions list, panel titles, panel assignment) with real condition1/condition2 names (swap-safe sentinels). bases1*=condition1, bases2*=condition2. Validated: transforms py_compile for default+swapped, dry-run enabled-default/enabled-swapped/disabled all 0 errors.

title: Make JACUSA2 optional via config differential-condition; skip when absent
description: rule jacusa2 (tools.smk) hard-codes WT_/ADAR1KO_ BAM groups; JACUSA2 outputs are always in rule all and always parsed. Add optional config key jacusa2_comparison:{condition1,condition2}. When present: rule jacusa2 contrasts those two condition groups, and JACUSA2 targets (Jacusa.out, Data_JACUSA2.json, JACUSA2_Table.csv) are produced. When absent: skip JACUSA2 entirely (not in rule all, not staged/parsed; Multiple-Analysis.py must not require Data_JACUSA2.json). Depends on parser fix.
close_reason: Fixed: HISAT2 idempotent chr-prepend + JACUSA2 dropna(how=all)+fillna via runtime patcher; JACUSA2 gated on config jacusa2_comparison (skip when absent). title: Fix JACUSA2 parser collapsing WT==ADAR1KO (drops differential sites)
description: JACUSA2.py _preprocess_jacusa_raw: dropna(subset=['wt','adarko']) drops any site where one condition lacks an ALT base - exactly the WT-edited/KO-unedited ADAR signal. Combined with <=2-distinct-base filter, every surviving site has identical dominant edit in both conditions -> WT and ADAR1KO rows byte-identical (verified 0/5683 rows differ). Fix via patcher: dropna(how='all') + fillna('') so single-condition sites are retained and counted toward the correct condition. Keep submodule pristine.
close_reason: Fixed: HISAT2 idempotent chr-prepend + JACUSA2 dropna(how=all)+fillna via runtime patcher; JACUSA2 gated on config jacusa2_comparison (skip when absent). Validated: patch transforms py_compile, real-data WT/KO recovered (2->4.5M differing rows), dry-run enabled=3 jacusa jobs / disabled=0 jacusa refs.

title: Fix HISAT2 double-chr prefix in downstream parsers (0% REDIportal artifact)
description: Downstream parsers BCFtools.py:60-61, REDItools2.py:35, SPRINT.py:36 unconditionally prepend 'chr' for the hisat2 aligner (line[0]='chr'+line[0]). HISAT2 was aligned to a chr-prefixed reference, so raw beds already have chr1 -> becomes chrchr1 -> zero overlap with REDIportal/Alu/HEK293T DB. Result: every HISAT2 REDIportal/Alu/SNP column is artificially 0 for BCFTools, REDItools2/3, SPRINT. Proof: RED-ML/JACUSA2 parsers lack this line and report correct nonzero HISAT2 numbers. Fix via the runtime patcher in rules/morales_downstream.smk: make the prepend idempotent (only prepend when not already startswith chr). Keep submodule pristine.
close_reason: Fixed: HISAT2 idempotent chr-prepend + JACUSA2 dropna(how=all)+fillna via runtime patcher; JACUSA2 gated on config jacusa2_comparison (skip when absent). Validated: patch transforms py_compile, real-data WT/KO recovered (2->4.5M differing rows), dry-run enabled=3 jacusa jobs / disabled=0 jacusa refs.

Caller FLAGS are now verified correct vs container --help (reditools2 -l=MIN_COLUMN_LENGTH, reditools3 -l=MIN_READ_DEPTH, jacusa2 -c/-q, REDItoolDnaRna -c/-q/-m comma-pairs). title: compare_outputs.py: write stub outputs for empty aligners (avoid missing-output failure)
description: scripts/compare_outputs.py process_aligner() does 'if not tools: print(...); return' -> returns WITHOUT writing the 6 per-aligner files the compare_outputs rule declares. If stream_records finds no columns for an aligner, Snakemake fails with 'missing output files'. Won't trigger when all aligners produce tool output (normal case), but is latent fragility. Fix: write empty/stub TSVs for that aligner instead of returning. Verified working on real small-example matrices (reditools~reditools3 site_fraction r=0.991), so this is hardening, not a live break.

value: Morales_et_al_small consensus analysis: 'non-consensus' edit sites are 99.2% JACUSA2-only statistical calls (3219/3244 private sites); only 0.5% of private sites have any real read depth vs 100% of consensus(>=3 tool) sites. ML tools redinet/red_ml are structurally subsets of REDItools candidates (redinet 100%, red_ml 81%) so they cannot call jacusa2/bcftools-only sites; among 1513 reditools candidates they flag only 23, selecting high edit-fraction (median EF 0.98 vs 0.03) regardless of depth. redinet positively endorses only 3/11 (labels 8 as SNP). SPRINT (14 sites, 7 private, support reads med=1) uses independent hyper-editing/SNV-cluster detection with no shared candidate list, so it is orthogonal. reditools3 is an exact duplicate of reditools. Analysis: results/correlation/consensus_analysis/

Permissivity verification (Morales_et_al_small, compare_all_tools matrices): site counts jacusa2=4848 > jacusa2_call1=1756 > reditools=1513 > bcftools=109 > red_ml=16 > sprint=14 > redinet=11. CLAIM 'JACUSA2 most permissive/sensitive' = VERIFIED (argmax volume; only 34% of its calls corroborated; jacusa2_call1 accepts ~100x lower edit fraction, median EF 0.0018 vs reditools 0.040). CLAIM 'SPRINT most stringent' = VERIFIED among de-novo callers (argmin of {jacusa2,jacusa2_call1,reditools,sprint}); redinet/red_ml are absolutely smaller but are downstream classifiers not de-novo callers. Summary doc: docs/consensus_permissivity_analysis.md; figures docs/figures/consensus_analysis/{consensus_vs_private,sprint_ml_dropout,tool_permissivity}.png

MARINE under SLURM+apptainer: marine_by_chrom MUST export TMPDIR to config.tmpdir (bound lustre path). SLURM sets $TMPDIR=node-local /scratch/$USER/job_<id> which the tscc2 profile apptainer-args does NOT bind (only binds /tscc/projects,/tscc/nfs/home,/tscc/lustre,/cm). MARINE's internal sort spills large edit sets to $TMPDIR -> 'sort: cannot create temporary file ... No such file or directory' -> fails ONLY on contigs big enough to spill (intermittent: 17/18 small-example marine jobs passed, only bwa/ADAR1KO_clone3 chrX failed). Same pattern other rules use (export TMPDIR={params.tmpdir}). Full small-example run verified complete: 18/18 marine outputs, marine present as 18 cols in compare_all_tools matrices (1193/5315 rows nonzero), aligner_correlation_marine + bigbed produced.

CORRECTION on ML tool inputs (Morales_et_al pipeline, rules/tools.smk): redinet and red_ml are wired DIFFERENTLY. redinet (rule redinet, tools.smk:523) takes a REDItools outTable.gz as input (tools.smk:527) and classifies only those rows -> 100% subset of REDItools is CODE-ENFORCED via the reditools_redinet_by_chrom->join->bgzip chain (tools.smk:410+). red_ml (rule red_ml, tools.smk:240) takes only the rmdup BAM (tools.smk:242) and runs red_ML.pl --rnabam, doing its OWN detection then filtering by dbSNP/simpleRepeat/Alu/p-value; it is NOT constrained to REDItools candidates. The 81% red_ml-vs-reditools overlap is EMERGENT, not structural (3/16 red_ml sites fall outside reditools). Supersedes earlier claim that red_ml is structurally a reditools subset.

MARINE integration (Morales_et_al, branch feature/marine_integration): container marine.sif, env 'marine', entrypoint /opt/conda/envs/marine/bin/python /opt/marine/marine.py (NOT /opt/marine/bin/MARINE/). MUST export NUMBA_CACHE_DIR+MPLCONFIGDIR (numba/matplotlib cache fails under RO HOME). Rule chain in rules/tools.smk: split_marine_md_bam_by_chrom -> marine_by_chrom (--contigs {chrom} on per-chrom MD bam, --cores=threads, --paired_end iff is_paired()) -> join_marine_output (gzip) -> filter_marine_by_edit_type. MARINE emits ALL 12 conversions genome-wide (~1855 sites/sample in small example); filter keeps strand_conversion==config edit_type ('AG'->'A>G', 204 sites). Edit type is BAKED INTO filename (final_filtered_site_info.AG.tsv) because TSCC profile uses rerun-triggers:mtime so params-trigger won't fire. Output cols: site_id barcode contig position ref alt strand count coverage conversion strand_conversion (NO edit_frequency col; frac=count/coverage). parse_marine/to_bed_marine fixed accordingly. marine added to _BED_TOOLS.
